# How our GFC 600H helps helicopter pilots fly smarter


September 9, 2026


## *Garmin’s flight control system for helicopters makes flying easier, even in demanding conditions*


Helicopter operations demand a lot. Complicated missions, adverse weather, complex environments and high workload are part of the job for even the most experienced pilot.


Whether you’re a helicopter owner or fleet operator, you need technology that works as hard as your team does. The Garmin[GFC™ 600H flight control system](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/625023/#overview) was designed with one goal in mind: to support the skilled helicopter pilot by making their job less fatiguing.


## Supporting pilots with helicopter-tailored features


Flying a helicopter takes a high level of skill that’s refined and mastered over time. But beyond stick-and-rudder demands, helicopter pilots are also simultaneously managing navigation, situational awareness, communications and mission execution. That’s where GFC 600H becomes an incredible asset.


GFC 600H provides advanced digital automation features — including attitude hold with speed stability, hover assist, Helicopter Stability and Protection (Garmin H-ESP™) technology, automatic return-to-level (LVL) mode and more — that help the helicopter pilot reduce fatigue. This allows the pilot to stay focused on executing the mission at hand. Cyclic-mounted controls allow easy engagement of the system’s primary functions without taking a hand off the controls.


## Stability where it counts


At its core, GFC 600H is an attitude-based flight control system built on advanced AHRS technology with redundant, cross-checking sensors. Key features include:


- **Garmin H-ESP** — Works continuously, even when the system isn’t engaged, to help maintain a stable flight condition. The H-ESP keeps the helicopter within an envelope and at appropriate pitch, roll and airspeed levels. It can be manually disabled for tactical maneuvers.
- **LVL mode** — Automatically recovers the aircraft from unusual attitudes and returns it to straight-and-level flight.
- **Hover assist** — Automatically provides inputs to help maintain position when hovering. Add the available yaw axis servo and it holds heading in hover too.
- **Overspeed and low speed protection** — Actively manages airspeed limits in both directions, with Low-G protection also available for the Bell 505.


## Seamless integration with Garmin avionics


The sought-after stability features of the GFC 600H don’t operate in isolation. The system integrates with feature-rich compatible Garmin avionics, including[G500H TXi™ flight displays](https://www.garmin.com/en-CA/p/625427/) ,[GTN™ Xi series navigators](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/606798/pn/010-02002-05/) ,[GI 275 attitude indicator](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/898837/pn/010-GI275-11/) and[GNC® 215 NAV/COMM radio](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/721525/pn/010-02481-02/) . For en route and approach navigation, compatible WAAS-enabled navigators like the GTN Xi series and[G1000H® NXi integrated flight deck](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/625024/) allow the system to automatically fly lateral and vertical flight paths, including search and rescue patterns, visual approaches, altitude hold, vertical speed and more.


## Flexible configuration and helicopter availability


GFC 600H supports both 2-axis and 3-axis configurations, features an NVG-compatible mode controller and is backed by our industry-leading product support team. Supplemental type certification has been completed for a variety of helicopters. GFC 600H was made available for Airbus H130 and is also available on[a variety of different models](https://www.garmin.com/en-CA/p/625023/#additional) .
